name: nano-dbf22c70-blind19-ots
instr:
# nano: nineteen quiet regressions to diagnose without a test suite

I moved my realtime game backend onto a recent checkout of this framework — it is what brings my listening ports up, keeps track of who is playing, and carries calls from one running copy of my game to another — and almost everything I touch now answers slightly wrong. Nothing about my own code changed, so I wrote down exactly what I did and what came back. The repository has received 19 separate undocumented edits.

Bringing the thing up, and getting a call through to the code meant to answer it, both fail now. A setup that used to come up fine aborts before serving anything, complaining that an address it is supposed to advertise is empty. When one running copy passes a request along to another, the step that obtains the outbound link hands back nothing at all even after that link has been opened successfully, and the caller falls over on the nothing it was given. After I register an object so its request entry points become callable, those entry points are no longer recognised as such: calls that used to work are turned away as unknown, while functions never meant to be reachable get exposed.
